DEFINITION · qeva:1:quasiperiodicity@1

Quasiperiodicity

A context-dependent torus-frequency representation often used for recurrent behavior with several incommensurate frequencies.

editorialdynamics · analysis · sequence
Run a related experimentTrace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

A common quasiperiodic model combines several angular motions whose basic frequencies are rationally independent. The representation itself must be distinguished from the extra conditions needed to guarantee that the resulting function is nonperiodic.

EXACT

The compact statement

Under this convention, f:R->X has a quasiperiodic torus representation when f(t)=F(theta_0+omega t), where F:T^k->X, theta_0 in T^k, and omega in R^k. A commonly imposed nonresonance condition is rational independence of the components of omega: m·omega=0 for m in Z^k implies m=0. Nonperiodicity of f does not follow from that condition alone if F has additional symmetries or degeneracies.

Example

f(t)=cos(t)+cos(sqrt(2)t) is nonperiodic and has a two-frequency quasiperiodic representation under this convention.

Boundary / caveat

“Quasiperiodic” has other precise meanings in tilings, symbolic dynamics, cocycles, and other areas. Each use must state its convention.

Assumptions

  • F:T^k→X is periodic in each angular coordinate, where T=R/(2πZ).
  • ω in R^k is a frequency vector.
